claim: Hugging Face's strategy-selection table says: single node / model fits on one GPU -> DistributedDataParallel or ZeRO; doesn't fit -> PipelineParallel, ZeRO or TensorParallel; largest layer doesn't fit -> TensorParallel or ZeRO.
stance_target: the repo's claim that DDP is the default topology when the model fits replicated on each card
scope_conditions: Single-node multi-GPU setups; HF Transformers docs (main branch)
quoted_support: | single node/multi-GPU | fits on single GPU | DistributedDataParallel or ZeRO | ... | doesn't fit on single GPU | PipelineParallel, ZeRO or TensorParallel | ... | largest model layer doesn't fit | TensorParallel or ZeRO |

claim: DDP is recommended over single-machine DataParallel because it reduces communication overhead between GPUs, uses each GPU efficiently and scales beyond one machine.
stance_target: the repo's claim that DDP is the cheapest communication topology per step
scope_conditions: PyTorch DP vs DDP; multi-GPU and multi-machine
quoted_support: DDP is recommended because it reduces communication overhead between GPUs, efficiently utilizes each GPU, and scales to more than one machine.

claim: Model, pipeline and tensor parallelism all add inter-GPU communication overhead that can become the bottleneck, and the docs give no guidance for PCIe-only, no-P2P fabrics — so this source cannot support the repo's stronger claim that DDP is the *only* viable topology on this box.
stance_target: the boundary of what the HF docs can be cited for
scope_conditions: HF Transformers 'Parallelism methods' page, ~1.4k words, no benchmarks
quoted_support: Like other parallelism methods though, tensor parallelism adds communication overhead between GPUs. ... Passing results between GPUs also adds communication overhead and it can be a bottleneck.
